**Finding: Compliant** (no redline proposed)

The Agreement contains no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation binding us as Licensee:

- **License is expressly non-exclusive both ways** (Preamble, p0030, p0043, p0049) — Licensor may license to others, and nothing obliges us to source our FX platform or related services solely from Licensor.
- **Article II restrictions (p0035–p0047) and Article VI (p0085)** limit only how we use, disclose or transfer *Licensor's* Licensed Technology — standard IP-protection covenants, not exclusive dealing. No "sole and exclusive provider", "all of its requirements", or "shall not procure … from any third party" language exists anywhere in the document.
- **"Field of Use" (p0007)** uses the word "exclusive" only to scope permitted use of the Platform (Spot FX market data/orders); it does not restrict our freedom to buy elsewhere.
- **Article XXII Right of First Refusal (p0139)** — flagged by the planner hint — turns out to be a first-look right over a sale of assets or merger of Licensee, i.e. a change-of-control constraint rather than a procurement exclusivity. It is out of scope for EXCLUSIVITY, though I have noted it in the rationale as a candidate issue for the change-of-control/assignment rule (it pairs with the automatic-termination-on-change-of-control provision at p0134).

Our preferred position (no exclusivity on Customer) is already satisfied, so no edit was made.
